settings.title: Barreletics vs Grip Socks
settings.hero_subtitle: The grip sock fails two ways simultaneously. Performance Skins solve both. One pair replaces every grip sock you'll ever buy.
settings.double_failure_heading: The Double Failure of Grip Socks
settings.failure_1_text: Silicone dots are a surface application. With friction and heat from studio use, they peel, flake, and lose adhesion. Most grip socks lose meaningful grip within 6-8 weeks of regular use.
settings.failure_2_text: Fabric absorbs perspiration during class. Moisture sits between your foot and the floor, reducing grip at the exact moment you need it most — during intense holds and transitions.

settings.question: Are Barreletics really better than grip socks?
settings.answer: Yes, in every measurable category: grip longevity (cannot peel off), hygiene (non-porous, rinse clean), cost (one-time $74 vs $112-144/year), and lifespan (18+ months vs 6-8 weeks). The only trade-off is the upfront cost, which pays for itself within the first year.

settings.question: How much do grip socks actually cost per year?
settings.answer: At $14-18 per pair and replacing every 6-8 weeks (as most regular practitioners do), that's 6-8 pairs per year — totaling $112-144 annually. Barreletics cost $74 once and last 18+ months minimum.

settings.question: Why do grip socks stop working?
settings.answer: Two reasons: (1) The silicone dots are a surface application that peels and wears off with friction. (2) The fabric absorbs sweat during class, creating a moisture barrier between your foot and the surface — reducing grip when you need it most.

settings.question: Can I still use Barreletics at studios that require grip socks?
settings.answer: Barreletics serve the same purpose as grip socks — protecting studio equipment and providing grip. Studio policies vary, so check with your studio if you're unsure.

settings.question: What if I don't like them — can I return?
settings.answer: 30-day returns on items in new, sellable condition. Try them on indoors to check fit before your first studio session.
